question.worked_solution:
First, notice that all of the terms have a common factor of ${y}^{2}.$ To simplify the computation, we can factor out the ${y}^{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{y}^{4}-12{y}^{3}+9{y}^{2} & ={y}^{2}(4{y}^{2}-12y+9)\end{aligned}
$$

The expression $4{y}^{2}-12y+9$ is a perfect square trinomial that can be factored as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}(4{y}^{2}-12y+9) & = \\ {y}^{2}((2y)^{2}-12y+{3}^{2}) & = \\ {y}^{2}((2y)^{2}-2\cdot 3\cdot (2y)+{3}^{2}) & = \\ {y}^{2}(2y-3)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
